tagline: One of the world's largest global alternative asset management firms
hero_kpi_rationale: Fee-earning AUM is the primary driver of recurring and predictable revenues for Carlyle, reflecting the underlying base on which management fees are earned. It is a key indicator of the structural health of the business model, particularly in the context of asset manager valuations.

kpis.name: Fee-earning AUM
kpis.explanation: Amount of assets for which Carlyle earns management fees.
kpis.description: Total fee-generating assets in 2025, broken down by segments Private Equity ($101.4B), Credit ($169.5B), and AlpInvest ($66.0B).

kpis.name: Total AUM
kpis.explanation: Total value of assets managed by Carlyle for its funds and clients.
kpis.description: Total AUM of $476.8 billion as of December 31, 2025, distributed across Private Equity ($163.5B), Credit ($211.3B), and AlpInvest ($102.0B).
kpis.signal: Significant scale in the private markets

kpis.name: Gross IRR
kpis.explanation: Annualized return generated by funds before fees and carried interest.
kpis.description: Average gross IRR of Global Credit Carry funds at 11% across the portfolio. A measure of past performance, not forward-looking.
kpis.signal: Historical performance of Global Credit Carry funds

kpis.name: MOIC
kpis.explanation: Total value generated relative to invested capital in funds.
kpis.description: MOIC of 1.3x for all Global Credit Carry funds, indicating a 30% return on invested capital.

kpis.name: Net Accrued Carry
kpis.explanation: Carlyle's share of fund profits earned as the manager.
kpis.description: Net accrued carried interest of $263 million for Global Credit Carry funds, reflecting realized performance not yet distributed.
kpis.signal: Variable revenue linked to fund performance

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Number of employees employed by the firm.
kpis.description: Approximately 2,300 employees globally, representing the firm's management and advisory capacity.

kpis.name: AI Capex Growth
kpis.explanation: Annualized growth rate of capital expenditures related to artificial intelligence, particularly in data centers and technology infrastructure.
kpis.description: Annualized growth of 30% in portfolio technology spending, primarily driven by investments in AI and data centers. Proprietary portfolio data as of December 31, 2025.

kpis.name: Data Center Shipments Growth
kpis.explanation: Growth ratio of data center hardware shipment volumes compared to 2021.
kpis.description: Data center hardware shipments are 7.5 times higher than in 2021, supported by the wave of generative AI and cloud infrastructure investments. Source: public data and Carlyle portfolio analysis.
kpis.signal: Explosion in demand for AI infrastructure

risks.title: Subjective asset valuations and potential errors
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Item 1A, the language is direct about subjective judgments and potential valuation errors. This risk directly impacts reported fund performance and performance allocations (carry).

risks.title: Impairment of equity method investments
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A details the risk of impairment of equity method investments, notably the investment in NGP which experienced a significant write-down. Fundraising challenges and changes in economic arrangements are contributing impairment factors.

risks.title: Market volatility impacting performance allocations
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A highlights the significant impact of fair value fluctuations on performance allocations (carry). Portfolio volatility can generate multi-billion dollar swings in performance revenues.

risks.title: Foreign exchange risk on foreign assets and revenues
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A quantifies the impact of a 10% depreciation of foreign currencies on management fees and performance allocations. The firm's significant international exposure makes this risk material, though less existential than others.

risks.title: Interest rate risk on variable-rate borrowings
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A mentions variable-rate obligations under CLOs and quantifies the impact of a 1% increase in interest rates. The estimated financial impact is moderate, and exposure is managed through balance sheet structure.

risks.title: Credit risk related to derivative counterparties
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A identifies credit risk from derivative counterparties and financial institutions. The firm seeks to minimize this risk by limiting exposure per counterparty and using netting agreements.

risks.title: Impairment of intangible assets and goodwill
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A provides detailed discussion on the valuation of intangible assets and goodwill, requiring significant judgments and estimates. The risk of impairment is clearly stated, with annual reviews and ad hoc tests required.

ai_positioning.summary: While Carlyle does not position AI as a centralized internal strategy, the firm identifies significant investment opportunities linked to AI. The company emphasizes that its portfolio investments benefit from the exponential growth in AI spending (notably data centers at +30% annualized) and acknowledges the transformative impact of generative AI across investment sectors.
evidence: Technology spending growth at record 30% annualized rate driven by AI-related investment
Data center hardware shipments 7.5x higher than 2021 levels
Concerns regarding AI bubble intensified in November 2025; software sector down 33% YTD 2026
Concentration of AI capex particularly in data center infrastructure and AI product offerings
